content_html:
Job offers, pay stubs and budgets all quote pay in different units. A recruiter mentions an hourly rate, your employer pays every two weeks and your rent is due monthly. This salary calculator turns any one of those figures into all the others, so you can compare offers and plan a budget on the same footing. It works with gross pay, before taxes and deductions.

How to use the salary calculator

  1. Pay amount and paid per: enter the figure you know and choose its period, from hourly through annual.
  2. Hours per week and days per week: your normal schedule. These link hourly and daily pay to weekly and yearly pay. A standard full-time schedule is 40 hours over 5 days.
  3. Holidays and vacation days per year: days you do not work. They only affect the adjusted column, explained below.

How the conversion works

The calculator first turns your pay into an annual figure, then divides it back out:

  • Hourly pay × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual pay
  • Daily pay × days per week × 52 weeks = annual pay
  • Weekly × 52, bi-weekly × 26, semi-monthly × 24, monthly × 12 and quarterly × 4 = annual pay

Bi-weekly and semi-monthly are easy to mix up. Bi-weekly means every two weeks, which is 26 paychecks a year, so two months each year contain a third paycheck. Semi-monthly means twice a month, usually on fixed dates, which is 24 paychecks a year. The same salary gives a slightly smaller bi-weekly check than a semi-monthly one.

Unadjusted and adjusted pay

The unadjusted column assumes you are paid for all 52 weeks, which is how salaried jobs with paid holidays and paid vacation work. The adjusted column takes holidays and vacation out of the working year. Working days are 52 × days per week, minus holidays and vacation days.

  • If you are paid by the hour or the day, the adjusted annual figure shows what you would earn if that time off is unpaid. This is useful for contractors, freelancers and hourly jobs without paid leave.
  • If you are paid a fixed salary, your yearly pay stays the same, but it is earned over fewer hours. The adjusted hourly rate shows what each hour you actually work is worth.

Worked example

Take the default inputs: $30 an hour, 40 hours over 5 days a week, 10 holidays and 15 vacation days.

FigureCalculationResult
Annual pay$30 × 40 × 52$62,400
Monthly pay$62,400 ÷ 12$5,200
Bi-weekly pay$62,400 ÷ 26$2,400
Days worked52 × 5 − 10 − 15235
Adjusted annual pay$30 × 8 hours × 235 days$56,400

If those 25 days off are unpaid, the year is worth $6,000 less. Going the other way, a $75,000 salary is $36.06 an hour over 2,080 paid hours, but $39.89 for each of the 1,880 hours actually worked.

Tips for comparing pay

  • When comparing an hourly contract with a salaried job, compare the contract's adjusted annual pay with the salary, since contractors are rarely paid for time off.
  • Add the value of benefits to a salaried offer. Health insurance, retirement matching and paid leave can be worth thousands of dollars a year.
  • Self-employed workers pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare, so a contract rate needs to be noticeably higher than an employee's hourly wage to come out even.
  • A year is slightly more than 52 weeks, so a calendar year occasionally holds 27 bi-weekly paydays. Annual figures here use exactly 52 weeks.

To see what lands in your bank account after federal tax, Social Security, Medicare and deductions, run your annual figure through a take-home pay calculator.

faq.question: How many working hours are in a year?
faq.answer: A full-time schedule of 40 hours a week for 52 weeks is 2,080 paid hours. After 10 holidays and 15 vacation days, the hours actually worked drop to about 1,880.

faq.question: Is $25 an hour a good salary?
faq.answer: At 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, $25 an hour is $52,000 a year before tax. Whether that is enough depends on your local cost of living, household size and benefits, so compare it with your expected monthly expenses.

faq.question: Does this salary calculator include taxes?
faq.answer: No. Every figure is gross pay before federal and state income tax, Social Security, Medicare and any deductions. Use a take-home pay calculator to estimate your net paycheck.

faq.question: How do I convert a monthly salary to an hourly rate?
faq.answer: Multiply the monthly amount by 12 to get annual pay, then divide by the hours you are paid for in a year. For example, $5,000 a month is $60,000 a year, or about $28.85 an hour over 2,080 hours.

faq.question: Should I count overtime in the hours per week?
faq.answer: Only if you work it regularly and are paid the same rate for it. Overtime is usually paid at one and a half times the normal rate, so for an accurate figure convert your base pay here and add expected overtime pay separately.
